summary: Okta consent re-prompt prevents headless Terraform deployer from creating service tokens
description: Issue summary: After an Okta OAuth app consent policy change rolled on 2026-03-09, our headless Terraform deployer (gitlab-runner-managed service) started failing to acquire tokens. The IdP now requires interactive user consent in some flows which causes headless token creation to fail with 'consent_required' / 400 responses. This prevents automated provisioning pipelines from creating ephemeral service tokens used by infrastructure jobs.
impact: Automated infra provisioning and nightly environment spin-ups fail across multiple repos. ~12 scheduled jobs failed in the last 24h; devs must manually create tokens to run deploys. No customer-facing outage, but developer productivity and CI automation are blocked.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger Terraform deployer job which uses the headless OAuth flow to mint an ephemeral service token.
2) Observe token-service receives 400 from Okta: {"error":"consent_required", "error_description":"End-user consent is required"}.
3) Job aborts with 'failed to obtain token' and returns HTTP 400 to the runner.
4) Manually re-running the same job from a dev account that previously performed interactive consent succeeds (demonstrates consent gating).
logs: 2026-03-11T02:13:04Z token-service ERROR requestId=abc123 okta_response=400 consent_required End-user consent is required
2026-03-11T02:13:04Z deployer WARN jobId=infra-provision-421 failed to obtain ephemeral token: oauth_error=consent_required
Okta audit: 2026-03-09T18:00:00Z: OAuth app policy updated: 'Require end-user consent' toggled to true for Web and Native flows (admin: okta-admin@redwood.com)
investigation_notes: - Confirmed Okta policy change on 2026-03-09 via system audit logs. The change applied to the 'Redwood Deployments' OAuth app and added a consent requirement for flows that do not have prior approval.

- Headless deployer uses an OAuth client credential-like flow implemented by our token-service which expects silent token grant; Okta treats the flow as requiring user consent because the app was marked to require consent for access to a scoping scope 'redwood.service.write'.
- Reproduced in staging by toggling consent flag on the test app and running headless flow: same 'consent_required' error returned.
- Workaround: granting org-level consent for the OAuth app (via Okta Admin > Applications > Grant admin consent) allows headless tokens to be minted without interactive prompt.

- Hypothesis: recent Okta setting change (intentional by security team) was rolled without back-compat check for machine flows. We need either an allowed 'client_credentials' style grant or pre-approved consent for the service accounts used by CI.

- Potential mitigation paths evaluated: 1) Admin pre-approve app scopes in Okta (fast); 2) Update token-service to use client_credentials (requires Okta app reconfiguration and PR changes); 3) Create dedicated machine-to-machine app with client_credentials and rotate secrets (more secure but higher effort).
comments: Maya Chen (2026-03-10): Raised after infra runbook owner flagged repeated CI failures overnight. Added initial logs and Okta audit link.

Diego Alvarez (2026-03-11): Investigated and reproduced in staging. Confirmed 'consent_required' from Okta. Short-term: will request admin consent in Okta for the app and confirm CI resumes. Long-term: propose creating a client_credentials app for machine flows.
SRE Team (2026-03-11): Suggest granting org-level consent as emergency mitigation. Also flagged potential policy drift by Identity team; please coordinate before changing global consent.

Identity Security (2026-03-12): We did roll a tighter consent policy to limit broad delegations. We can provide a scoped exception for the 'Redwood Deployments' app after justification and change control. Please submit change request to identity-runbook channel with a brief justification.
resolution: In progress: emergency admin consent was granted for the 'Redwood Deployments' app by Identity Security on 2026-03-12 to restore CI. Token issuance resumed and affected jobs completed. Follow-up task created to migrate headless deployer to a dedicated client_credentials Okta app (INT-314889). Additional change request submitted to identity-runbook for documented exception and audit trail.
